ranking_source.name: CloudSEK
ranking_source.title: Top 10 Advanced Persistent Threat (APT) Groups in 2026
ranking_source.note: Order follows CloudSEK's ranking of groups that dominated 2025 via large-scale espionage, identity attacks, and infrastructure access. Summaries are enriched from MITRE ATT&CK, CISA, and 2025–2026 public reporting.

actors.name: Salt Typhoon
actors.summary: PRC state-backed actor that lives inside carrier and ISP gear — Cisco and other edge boxes — to tap traffic at scale. Active since at least 2019; MITRE tracks packet sniffing, GRE tunnels, and config theft on compromised network devices.
actors.campaign: 600+ organizations across 80+ countries, including nine U.S. telecoms and CALEA lawful-intercept systems. 2026 reporting adds South American carriers and new implants (TernDoor, PeerTime, BruteEntry).

actors.name: Flax Typhoon
actors.targets: Government, education, manufacturing, IT — Taiwan first, then global relays
actors.summary: China-based group that prefers living-off-the-land and legitimate remote-access tools over custom malware. Distinguished by turning hundreds of thousands of SOHO routers, cameras, and IoT boxes into a quiet relay botnet.
actors.campaign: DoJ/FBI disruption (2024) documented control of 260k+ devices worldwide, including hundreds of thousands of unique U.S. devices. CloudSEK still ranks the cluster among 2025's dominant APTs because the botnet model survived as espionage plumbing.

actors.name: Mustang Panda
actors.targets: Governments, NGOs, churches, maritime and Southeast Asian policy targets
actors.summary: High-tempo China-aligned espionage shop. Classic kit is PlugX / ToneShell delivered by themed lure documents, then USB worming to jump air-gapped or poorly segmented networks.
actors.campaign: Through 2025: Frankenstein ToneShell in Myanmar, Yokai backdoor against Royal Thai Police (LNK+PDF), and a shift toward USB as a second initial-access path beside phishing.

actors.name: APT17
actors.targets: U.S. government, defense, law firms, IT, mining, NGOs
actors.summary: Long-running China-based intrusion set (Deputy Dog / Aurora Panda). CloudSEK called out APT17 specifically for 2025 identity-centric operations — stealing and replaying credentials rather than burning custom implants.
actors.campaign: Historical hits on U.S. government and legal sector. 2025 dominance, per CloudSEK, came from large-scale identity attacks sitting alongside the Typhoon clusters rather than a single named worm.

actors.name: APT28
actors.targets: Defense ministries, political parties, media, war-adjacent orgs
actors.summary: GRU's most public intrusion set. Spearphish and exploit-driven, with a habit of burning fresh Office / WinRAR bugs against targets tied to European security and the Ukraine war.
actors.campaign: Trend Micro's 2026 H1 APT report: Pawn Storm weaponized a fresh Office zero-day within weeks and hit defense ministries through border police. Parallel Earth Dahu activity kept milking a known WinRAR flaw.

actors.name: APT29
actors.targets: Governments, diplomats, think tanks, cloud identity providers
actors.summary: SVR's patient cloud-and-identity hunter. Prefers token theft, OAuth abuse, and supply-chain or trusted-provider pivots over noisy malware. Dwell measured in months.
actors.campaign: Post-SolarWinds tradecraft never really left: password-spray and token replay against Microsoft 365 / Entra, plus diplomatic mailbox collection. CISA still lists Midnight Blizzard as an SVR APT in 2026 assessments.

actors.name: Sandworm
actors.targets: Energy, ICS/OT, government, Ukraine and NATO-adjacent infrastructure
actors.summary: GRU's destructive arm. Famous for BlackEnergy / NotPetya / Industroyer; in this cycle the signature is wiper malware against power and energy networks, not just espionage.
actors.campaign: 2025–2026: ZEROLOT wiper against Ukrainian energy, plus a failed wiper attempt on Polish energy systems. Opposite pole of Lazarus — impact over theft.

actors.name: Lazarus Group
actors.targets: Crypto exchanges, banks, defense, software supply chains
actors.summary: North Korea's flagship APT. Dual-hatted: classic espionage plus industrial-scale theft that funds the regime. Sub-clusters include APT38 (finance) and BlueNoroff (crypto / IT workers).
actors.campaign: Bybit heist (~$1.5B) via a Safe{Wallet} supply-chain compromise — largest single APT theft on record. Netlas cites ~$2.02B stolen in 2025. 2026 H1: BlueNoroff hit the Axios npm maintainer (100M+ weekly downloads).

actors.name: Kimsuky
actors.targets: South Korean government, U.S. policy shops, think tanks, journalists
actors.summary: DPRK's dedicated collection team. Lower dollar-value than Lazarus, higher volume of spearphish, credential harvest, and strategic documents aimed at Korean peninsula policy.
actors.campaign: Remains in every 2025–2026 'most active APT' list. Typical cycle: spoofed ministry mail, browser-in-the-middle or stealer, then mailbox rule persistence. Complements Lazarus cash operations with intelligence take.

actors.name: APT42
actors.targets: Journalists, academics, NGOs, dissidents, Gulf defense officials
actors.summary: IRGC-linked social-engineering specialist. Patient, personal, and mailbox-focused: fake journalists, conference invites, and cloud phishing rather than noisy network worms.
actors.campaign: SpearSpecter (Sep 2025) dropped TAMECAT on senior Gulf defense officials, including family-member targeting. Check Point and others describe an elevated 2026 tempo after regional strikes.
